headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, revenue trends are mixed while AI and tech investments remain a common focus.
summary: Media & Entertainment shows strong top‑line growth at Disney but weaker performance at Warner Bros. Discovery. Gaming revenues are led by Caesars, yet Bally shows the fastest growth. Publishing is split between Wolters Kluwer’s AI push and Scholastic’s revenue miss. Education companies are broadly positive, driven by Pearson’s growth and NYU’s quantum partnership.

industries.summary: Disney posted 7% revenue growth and a 21% rise in operating income. Warner Bros. Discovery’s Skydance raised its EBITDA outlook but saw a 13.4% revenue decline. Versant grew to $1.64 bn with stable margins.

leaders.why: Revenue $25,248 m and strong margin expansion

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney is hiring AI talent from Character.AI; Skydance is building AI‑driven content pipelines; Versant’s Fandango is expanding digital platforms.

themes.title: IT spend outlook
themes.detail: Disney expands IT spend, Skydance tightens, Versant’s outlook is unclear.

industries.it_note: Account teams should monitor Disney’s AI hiring wave and Skydance’s AI content initiatives for partnership opportunities.

industries.summary: Caesars reported $3.0 bn revenue but a net loss. Bally’s achieved 20% revenue growth. Light & Wonder secured a new vendor contract and Brightstar maintained stable margins.

themes.title: Vendor shifts
themes.detail: Light & Wonder won a new table‑games contract; Brightstar extended its New York Lottery tech deal.

themes.title: IT spend outlook
themes.detail: Light & Wonder is tightening spend; other firms have unclear or expanding outlooks.

industries.it_note: Focus on Light & Wonder’s cost‑tightening and Brightstar’s contract extensions for potential tech services.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer is expanding AI across its units. Scholastic missed revenue targets and posted a large operating loss. Pearson delivered modest revenue growth and margin improvement.

leaders.why: Revenue $1,779 m and margin up to 14.2%

themes.title: AI rollout
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer added AI tools to tax, legal and health products; Pearson launched AI‑centric learning tools.

themes.title: IT spend outlook
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer is expanding IT spend; Scholastic is tightening; Pearson’s outlook is unclear.

industries.it_note: Account teams should align with Wolters Kluwer’s AI expansion while watching Scholastic’s cost cuts.

industries.summary: Pearson posted 4% revenue growth and higher operating profit. NYU secured multi‑hundred‑million dollar quantum funding. SLU expanded its AI partnership with World Wide Technology.

themes.title: Quantum & AI research
themes.detail: NYU received $284 m for a quantum fabrication facility and uses AI in archaeology; SLU deepened AI collaboration with WWT.

themes.title: IT spend outlook
themes.detail: NYU’s quantum lab signals expanding spend; Pearson’s outlook is unclear; other schools are neutral.

industries.it_note: Leverage NYU’s quantum initiative and Pearson’s AI learning tools for joint technology projects.
